Topics · Hard times

How do I live with fear for my child?

A father prepares, then entrusts; a mother places her daughter in God's shelter. No outcome is promised.

If you are in pain right now, you do not have to carry it alone. Please reach out to someone you trust, or to a local crisis line or emergency number. Find a helpline near you

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَقَالَ يَـٰبَنِىَّ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ مِنۢ بَابٍ وَٰحِدٍ وَٱدْخُلُوا۟ مِنْ أَبْوَٰبٍ مُّتَفَرِّقَةٍ ۖ وَمَآ أُغْنِى عَنكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ ۖ إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ ۖ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ ۖ وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ٦٧ وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُم مَّا كَانَ يُغْنِى عَنْهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِى نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَىٰهَا ۚ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِّمَا عَلَّمْنَـٰهُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ٦٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against [the decree of] Allāh at all. The decision is only for Allāh; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who would rely [indeed] rely." And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allāh at all except [it was] a need [i.e., concern] within the soul of Jacob, which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.

Quran · Yusuf 12:67-68

Translation

May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. If I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”

Original · Hebrew

וְאֵ֣ל שַׁדַּ֗י יִתֵּ֨ן לָכֶ֤ם רַחֲמִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָאִ֔ישׁ וְשִׁלַּ֥ח לָכֶ֛ם אֶת־אֲחִיכֶ֥ם אַחֵ֖ר וְאֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֑ין וַאֲנִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁכֹ֖לְתִּי שָׁכָֽלְתִּי׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 43:14

World English Bible

Jacob advises his sons not to enter by one gate but by separate gates. Then he says this will not avail them against God at all, and that he has put his trust in Him. A father takes care, then entrusts. The text describes a need in Jacob's soul that he carried out, and does not blame him for it. Care and entrusting do not clash in the verse. A parent's fear is a need of the soul, met and not denied.

A question for you

What is closest to what you feel?

If you sayI take great care and still find no ease.
ThenThat is what the text describes: a need in the soul. It does not ask you to put it out, only to hand over what lies beyond.
If you sayI fear what I cannot prevent.
ThenThe next step is a mother's prayer for her daughter, a prayer for what no one can prevent.
If you sayI feel I am falling short.
ThenThe father in the verse says plainly that he can guarantee nothing, and the verse does not fault him. This page does not fault you.

Part 2 of 3

﴿فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَضَعْتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلْأُنثَىٰ ۖ وَإِنِّى سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّىٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

But when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female." And Allāh was most knowing of what she delivered, and the male is not like the female. "And I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her in You and [for] her descendants from Satan, the expelled [from the mercy of Allāh]."

Quran · Aal Imran 3:36

Imran's wife says to her Lord after giving birth: I have borne a girl, and I have named her Mary, and I place her and her offspring in Your refuge. A mother puts her daughter and her daughter's children in God's shelter, speaking plainly to God about what was not as she had expected. Here is a ready form for any parent: to place the one you fear for in a refuge, by name.

A question for you

What would be easy for you to say?

If you sayOnly their name.
ThenThe name is enough. It is what the mother in the verse did.
If you sayI want to protect them from things I cannot name.
ThenYou may say that too: from all that I fear and cannot name.
If you sayI do not know whether prayer changes anything.
ThenThe verses do not claim what prayer does to an outcome. They claim that it was said.

Part 3 of 3

﴿يَـٰبُنَىَّ إِنَّهَآ إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ فَتَكُن فِى صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ أَوْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَأْتِ بِهَا ٱللَّهُ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[And Luqmān said], "O my son, indeed if it [i.e., a wrong] should be the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or [anywhere] in the heavens or in the earth, Allāh will bring it forth. Indeed, Allāh is Subtle[1162] and Aware.

Translator's notes

[1162] Refer to footnote of 6:103.

Quran · Luqman 31:16

Translation

For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֤י אֶת־כָּל־מַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים יָבִ֥א בְמִשְׁפָּ֖ט עַ֣ל כָּל־נֶעְלָ֑ם אִם־ט֖וֹב וְאִם־רָֽע׃

Ecclesiastes · 12:14

World English Bible

Luqman tells his son that anything, even the weight of a mustard seed, in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, God will bring it, and that God is gentle and aware. A father tells his son that what is too small to be seen is not hidden from God. So the one you fear for is not outside the sight of One who is gentle and aware. That does not mean nothing will touch them. It means they are not forgotten.

A question for you

What will you take to your son or daughter from this page?

If you sayTo listen to them more.
ThenThat is among the truest things a parent has.
If you sayTo pray for them each night.
ThenThat is close to what the mother in the verse did: she put her child in God's care, by name.
If you sayTo fear less.
ThenThat is not asked. Perhaps it is enough to fear with Someone carrying it with you.

Your reflection

What name will you say in your prayer tonight?
